item.title: The reverse isoperimetric inequality for convex shapes included in a triangle
item.description: arXiv:2610.36220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a sharp reverse isoperimetric inequality for convex subsets of a triangle under a prescribed area constraint. Given a triangle $T$ and an area fraction $\eta\in(0,1)$, we determine the set with maximal perimeter among convex bodies $K\subset T$ satisfying $|K|=\eta|T|$ and characterize the equality cases. Every maximizer is a triangle, and the optimal configuration is obtained by retaining a longest side of $T$ and placing the third vertex on a shortest side, at the position determined by the area constraint. This characterization yields an explicit expression for the maximal perimeter in terms of $\eta$ and the side lengths of $T$.
item.dc:creator: Rida Ait El Manssour, Zakaria Fattah, Ilias Ftouhi

item.title: An approximate inner ball condition characterizing $C^{1,\alpha}$ convex bodies
item.description: arXiv:2610.36238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main result of this paper uses an approximate inner ball condition to characterize $C^{1,\alpha}$ convex bodies for $0<\alpha\leq 1$. In particular, we show that a convex body $K$ is of class $C^{1,\alpha}$ if and only if there exist constants $C,\varepsilon_0>0$ such that for every $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0$ and for every $x\in\partial K$ there exists $h^\varepsilon(x)$ satisfying $B(h^\varepsilon(x), C\varepsilon^\frac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha})\subset K$ and $\operatorname{dist}(x,B(h^\varepsilon(x), C\varepsilon^\frac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha}))\leq\varepsilon.$ We then give a new proof of the regularity of the convex envelope by showing that $\operatorname{conv}(f)\in C^{1,\alpha}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ whenever $f\in C^{1,\alpha}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $f$ satisfies the coercivity condition $f(x)\to\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$. Finally, we use the approximate inner ball characterization of $C^{1,\alpha}$ convex bodies to prove that the Minkowski sum of a $C^{1,\alpha}$ convex body and a nonempty closed convex set is a $C^{1,\alpha}$ convex domain.
item.dc:creator: Anthony R. Cappello

item.title: Outer Lipschitz Geometry of Unions of Tangential Nodal Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.36381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2000, Birbrair and Fernandes proved that the H\"older Semicomplex of the branches of a germ of a curve with its contact orders is a complete invariant of outer bi-Lipschitz equivalence of definable sets in polynomially bounded o-minimal structures. They also proved a realization theorem for it, i.e., for each H\"older semicomplex $G$, there is a germ of a semialgebraic curve $(X,x_0)$ such that the H\"older Semicomplex of $(X,x_0)$ coincides with $G$. In 2000, Birbrair proposed the problem of finding and characterizing all the H\"older semicomplexes that can be realized as a H\"older Semicomplex of a real analytic curve. Solving this problem in its full generality is a notoriously hard task; however, in this paper, we provide a complete answer to this problem when we restrict it to tangential nodal curves: curves defined as the union of the zero set of a harmonic function and its tangent cone at a fixed point.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Edson Sampaio, Luan Moura Sousa, Emanoel Ferreira de Souza

item.title: New upper bounds for average kissing numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.36675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A packing of balls in Euclidean space is a set of balls with non-overlapping interiors. For a finite packing of balls, its average contact number is the average number of balls tangent to a ball in this packing, that is, twice the total number of tangencies divided by the number of balls. The average kissing number of the space is defined as the supremum of average contact numbers over all finite ball packings. In this paper, we present a new semidefinite programming approach to average kissing numbers and improve upon known upper bounds in all dimensions \(3\) through \(30\). In particular, we provide the first improvements to the upper bounds in dimensions \(10\) through \(30\) obtained from kissing numbers. We also fully solve the average kissing number problem in dimensions \(8\) and \(24\) by showing that the average kissing numbers coincide with the kissing numbers, 240 and 196560, respectively. These values are limits of average contact numbers of finite subpackings from the \(E_8\) and Leech lattices.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bockhaus, Alexey Glazyrin

item.title: On surfaces, that fill the space
item.description: arXiv:2610.36766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The article is devoted to the construction of dimension-raising maps of cubes with the highest possible Holder exponent. In particular, a square-to-cube mapping with a Holder exponent of $2/3$ is constructed, which is a solution to the V.I.Arnold problem.
item.dc:creator: E. V. Shchepin

item.title: Improved Brunn--Minkowski inequality for $\theta$-convolution bodies
item.description: arXiv:2610.37066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $n\geq 2$, we study the optimal function $\varphi_n$ in the Brunn-Minkowski inequality for $\theta$-convolution bodies $|K+_\theta L|^{1/n}\geq\varphi_n(\theta)(|K|^{1/n}+|L|^{1/n})$ for any convex bodies $K,L\subset\mathbb{R}^n$. We improve the known lower bound for every $0<\theta<(3/4)^n$ and determine $\varphi_n$ on an interval strictly containing $[(2/3)^n,1]$. For $\theta<1$ in this interval, equality holds if and only if $K$ and $-L$ are translates of the same $n$-dimensional simplex. The proof reduces the geometric problem to a sharp one-dimensional estimate for nonnegative concave functions under a weighted integral constraint.
item.dc:creator: Javier Mart\'in Go\~ni

item.title: Typical Kakeya-type sets and their typical code sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.37419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study properties of compact Besicovitch sets and other Kakeya-type sets which are typical in the sense that the exceptions form a meager set in the Baire category sense in a suitable metric space. The main motivation comes from the known fact that typical compact Besicovitch sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ have minimal Hausdorff dimension among all Besicovitch sets of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Thus, in order to estimate the smallest possible Hausdorff dimension of an arbitrary Besicovitch set, it is enough to estimate the Hausdorff dimension of a typical (compact) Besicovitch set, or analogously of a Besicovitch set satisfying our list of typical properties. Among other results, we prove that a typical Besicovitch set $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ has the following properties: it is not sticky, any line intersects $K$ in a set of ($1$-dimensional) measure zero or in a unit line segment and a set of measure zero, it has no more than $n$ different unit line segments in any direction, and for each $1\le j\le n$ the Hausdorff dimension of the set of those directions in which $K$ has exactly $j$ unit line segments is $n-j$. For compact metric spaces $X$ and $Y$, let $\mathcal{C}(X,Y)$ denote the set of compact subsets of $X\times Y$ whose projection onto the first coordinate is $X$, equipped with the Hausdorff metric. Kakeya-type compact sets can be coded by elements of such spaces, allowing typical properties to be studied through comeager subsets of $\mathcal C(X,Y)$. Among other results, we prove that, under suitable conditions on $X$ and $Y$, a typical $A\in \mathcal{C}(X,Y)$ is totally disconnected and purely unrectifiable, its projection to the second coordinate has Hausdorff dimension zero, and the dimension identities $\dim_H(A)=\dim_H(X)$ and $\dim_P(A)=\dim_P(X)+\dim Y$ hold.
item.dc:creator: Josef Bell, Ezekiel Fleissner-Kates, Tam\'as Keleti

item.title: Equidistant Affine Subspaces: Explicit Bounds, Codimension-Two Reduction, and Transverse Products
item.description: arXiv:2610.37421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}(k,n)$ be the largest size of a family of affine $k$-planes in $\R^n$ at pairwise separation distance one. We develop a unified treatment of upper bounds, dimension reduction, and product constructions. Orthogonal-projection coordinates give a rank-stratified distance identity; a Veronese lifting converts its polynomial consequences into simultaneous total isotropy. Connected Nash decomposition and an analytic diagonal argument replace the linear-independence step in H\"ofer's three-dimensional method. An explicit cylindrical decomposition estimate yields $\mathcal{N}(k,n)\leqslant 2^{\,2^{\,3(k+1)(n-k)}}$. For configurations whose direction sums have dimension at most $k+1$, we prove the exact reduction $\mathcal{N}_{\leqslant k+1}(k,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,n-k+1)$. Every codimension-two equidistant configuration splits off a common linear factor, giving $\mathcal{N}(n-2,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,3)$. We also determine the sharp bound $2(n-k)$ when all directions lie in a fixed $(k+1)$-dimensional subspace. A transverse product construction gives multiplicative inequalities and makes $S(c)=\mathcal{N}(c-1,2c-1)$ supermultiplicative. In particular, $S(c)\geqslant 2^{c\bmod 2}7^{\lfloor c/2\rfloor}$. The structural results and constructions do not depend on the exact value of $\mathcal{N}(1,3)$.
item.dc:creator: Jia Li

item.title: No Connectedness Lemma for Alexandrov spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.37476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since its introduction in 2003, Wilking's Connectedness Lemma has become a powerful tool in the study of manifolds with positive sectional curvature. In recent work of the authors, this has been extended to orbifolds. The purpose of this note is to exhibit counterexamples in the class of Alexandrov spaces for the Connectedness Lemma in both its ordinary and dual formulation. This answers a 2007 question of Wilking.
item.dc:creator: Jan Nienhaus, Dennis Wulle

item.title: Observable diameter of product measures with a power-type interior zero
item.description: arXiv:2610.35889v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the asymptotic order of the observable diameter of $\ell^p$-product spaces associated with a probability measure on $[0,1]$ whose density has a power-type interior zero. Different vanishing orders are allowed on the two sides of the zero. For every $1 \le p \le \infty$, we obtain sharp two-sided estimates and show that the asymptotic order is governed by the larger of the two vanishing orders. In the case $p=2$, the transition occurs exactly at the threshold for the spectral gap.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Shioya

item.title: $L^p$ Convergence of AMV Laplacians on completions of Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.36125v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study conditions for the $L^p$ convergence of the AMV Laplacian $\Delta_r$ on completions of Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$. The condition invloves the Minkowski dimension of the set $\overline{M} \setminus M$ and how much the curvature is blowing up around $S$. We build a concrete family of sets that satisfies these conditions, and provide an example of non convergence when these conditions are not met.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Dias

item.title: Shape optimization under minimal width and constant width constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.36382v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study shape optimization problems for planar convex sets with prescribed minimal width or constant width. We prove that the Reuleaux triangle minimizes torsional rigidity among sets of constant width. We also show that the first Dirichlet-Laplace eigenvalue is maximized by the equilateral triangle under a minimal width constraint and by the Reuleaux triangle under a constant width constraint. The proofs use subsets consisting of a disk and three straight or circular caps. Reflection arguments reduce the study to equilateral configurations, which contain a polygon or a disk polygon depending on one parameter. The same cap constructions give a common proof of the known area, Cheeger and inner parallel area inequalities, and yield sharp bounds for all positive moments of the distance to the boundary. We also prove sharp inequalities for concentric disk intersections and decreasing radial integrals, and compare interaction energies for kernels close to a positive constant. This includes a nonempty interval of positive Riesz exponents. Finally, we investigate whether inclusion monotonicity and Minkowski concavity suffice to obtain these comparisons for other functionals.
item.dc:creator: Beniamin Bogosel

item.title: Boundary Geometry Determines Optimal Shallow ReLU Approximation under Weighted Coefficient Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.36854v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how boundary geometry affects $L^q$ approximation by shallow ReLU neural networks on convex bodies $K\subset\mathbb R^d$. The target classes are unit balls of weighted variation spaces that can enlarge classical spaces by incorporating domain geometry into constraints on output coefficients. We establish upper and lower bounds for arbitrary convex bodies and determine the optimal polynomial approximation exponents for all planar convex bodies and their products with polytopes, including cubes and circular cylinders. For $C^2$ convex bodies, we determine the optimal exponents in a dimension-dependent range of $q$ extending beyond $2$. When all principal curvatures are positive, the result extends to every finite $q\ge2$. For these classes, the dependence of the optimal exponent on the domain is captured by a single geometric growth exponent associated with small boundary caps. We also identify sharp weight thresholds for retaining the classical approximation exponent and improve previous weights on Euclidean balls while preserving the classical $L^2$ approximation rate. When the target is given as a finite ReLU network, the upper bounds can be realized by a compressed network using only the original neurons, without increasing the weighted coefficient sum. These results show that boundary geometry can change the optimal exponent even when dimension, error norm, and weighting rule are fixed.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Qi Yang, Lei Shi

item.title: Fisher Completions and Statistical Regularization of Wrapped Gaussian Families
item.description: arXiv:2610.37526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the intrinsic Fisher completion of the full-covariance wrapped Gaussian family on a fixed torus and relate its geometry to uniform estimation. The completion is homeomorphic to the total-variation closure. Every added law is, in suitable integer torus coordinates, a product of a uniform law and a lower-dimensional wrapped Gaussian. All these densities are positive and real analytic, but in dimension at least two no added point has a compact neighborhood. Small balls remain contractible, and explicit minimizing geodesics pass through added points. In dimension at least two, every fixed Fisher neighborhood of an added point has a positive minimax risk at every sample size. For subfamilies with a common positive lower bound on the variance in every nonzero integer direction, we prove that compactness of the completed closure is equivalent to uniform consistency in either $L^1$ or completed-Fisher loss. Equivalently, the Fourier moments must decay uniformly over the subfamily. A fixed covariance floor guarantees this condition without an upper covariance bound and gives $L^1$ risk at most $C_{\varepsilon,d}n^{-1/2}\{\log(n+1)\}^{d/4}$. A common-phase example illustrates how partially uniform limits can retain relative-phase information while remaining uniformly estimable.
item.dc:creator: Gunhee Cho, Hyun Chul Jang

item.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincar\'e Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.37659v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a new functional inequality for uniformly log-concave measures, stronger than the Poincar\'e inequality. This new inequality bounds the variance of differences of convex functions and is motivated by the stability theory of optimal transport: for a fixed uniformly log-concave source measure, it provides a sharp stability bound for Brenier potentials with respect to variations of the target measure. Applying this inequality to Gaussian measures, we recover the fact that the Bures-Wasserstein distance between two positive semidefinite matrices is equivalent to the Frobenius distance between their square roots. Our proofs hinge upon linearization arguments for the Monge-Amp\`ere equation governing the quadratic optimal transport problem.
item.dc:creator: Cyril Letrouit, Tudor Manole

item.title: Hyperbolicity Beyond Convexity in the Alexandrov-Fenchel Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.08746v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an Alexandrov--Fenchel type inequality in which one of the reference bodies is replaced by a function whose Hessian satisfies a balancing condition on its eigenvalues, without being required to be positive semidefinite. The proof hinges on a new extension of Alexandrov's inequality for mixed discriminants. As applications, we derive a log-concavity principle for linear functionals of area measures, answering a question of Colesanti, Hug, and Saor\'in-G\'omez, as well as Brunn--Minkowski type inequalities for intrinsic volumes of mean section bodies, answering a question of Schuster.
item.dc:creator: Leo Brauner, Oscar Ortega-Moreno

item.title: Every Extended Metric Space Is Isometrically Embeddable into the Gromov-Hausdorff Class
item.description: arXiv:2610.24279v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{GH}$ denote the Gromov--Hausdorff class of isometry classes of nonempty metric spaces, equipped with the Gromov--Hausdorff extended pseudometric. We prove that every nonempty extended metric space is isometrically embeddable into $\mathfrak{GH}$. More precisely, for every nonempty extended metric space $X$, all image points may be represented by metrics on a common set of cardinality $\max\{\operatorname{dens} X,\aleph_0\}$. The main ingredient is a realization theorem for function spaces: for every nonempty set $I$, the space of all real-valued functions on $I$, endowed with the uniform extended metric, can be realized as a family of metrics on a fixed underlying set. Under this realization, the Gromov--Hausdorff distance agrees exactly with the uniform extended distance, including the case of infinite distance. The resulting metric spaces are complete, uniformly discrete, and unbounded, and have cardinality $\max\{|I|,\aleph_0\}$. If $I$ is countable, they may moreover be chosen proper and of bounded geometry. As further consequences, we obtain sharp cardinality results for clouds and universality results for cardinality-restricted parts of $\mathfrak{GH}$ and for spheres in the associated zero-distance quotients.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Fukano

item.title: Submanifolds with boundary in sub-Riemannian Heisenberg Groups
item.description: arXiv:2508.15634v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We discuss the notion of submanifolds with boundary with intrinsic $C^1$ regularity in sub-Riemannian Heisenberg groups and we provide some examples. Eventually, we present a Stokes' Theorem for such submanifolds involving the integration of Rumin's differential forms in Heisenberg groups.
item.dc:creator: Marco Di Marco, Davide Vittone

item.title: Combinatorial foundations for solvable chaotic local Euclidean quantum circuits in two dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2512.03029v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a graph-theoretic problem motivated by questions in quantum computing concerning the propagation of information in quantum circuits. A graph $G$ is said to be a bounded extension of its subgraph $L$ if they share the same vertex set, and the graph distance $d_L(u, v)$ is uniformly bounded for edges $uv\in G$. Given vertices $u, v$ in $G$ and an integer $k$, the geodesic slice $S(u, v, k)$ denotes the subset of vertices $w$ lying on a geodesic in $G$ between $u$ and $v$ with $d_G(u, w) = k$. We say that $G$ has bounded geodesic slices if $|S(u, v, k)|$ is uniformly bounded over all $u, v, k$. We call a graph $L$ geodesically directable if it has a bounded extension $G$ with bounded geodesic slices. Contrary to previous expectations, we prove that $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is geodesically directable. Physically, this provides a setting in which one could devise exactly-solvable chaotic local quantum circuits with non-trivial correlation patterns on 2D Euclidean lattices. In fact, we show that any bounded extension of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is geodesically directable. This further implies that all two-dimensional regular tilings are geodesically directable.
item.dc:creator: Fredy Yip

item.title: Prismatoid Band-Unfolding Revisited
item.description: arXiv:2603.09813v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It remains unknown if every prismatoid has a nonoverlapping edge-unfolding, a special case of the long-unsolved "D\"urer's problem." Recently nested prismatoids have been settled [Rad24] by mixing (in some sense) the two natural unfoldings, petal-unfolding and band-unfolding. Band-unfolding fails due to a specific counterexample [O'R13b]. The main contribution of this paper is a characterization when a band-unfolding of a nested prismatoid does in fact result in a nonoverlapping unfolding. In particular, we show that the mentioned counterexample is in a sense the only possible counterexample. Although this result does not expand the class of shapes known to have an edge-unfolding, its proof expands our understanding in several ways, developing tools that may help resolve the non-nested case.
item.dc:creator: Joseph O'Rourke

item.title: A BMO-type representation formula for the total variation of SBV functions in Heisenberg groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.35577v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a formula for the total variation of SBV functions in sub-Riemannian Heisenberg groups arising as the limit of certain BMO-type functionals.
item.dc:creator: Marco Di Marco, Sebastiano Don, Davide Vittone
